items.title: Efforts under way to keep pregnant 12-year-old in school
items.summary: Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the department would discuss the matter with the girl's family and school to determine how she could continue her studies, taking into account her health and ability. "We will discuss the matter with the family first. Nancy said the department would also assess the need for welfare support and psychosocial services for the girl and her family to help them cope with the situation.

items.title: Cobra surprises eatery operator in flood-hit kitchen
items.summary: Recounting the tense moment, Muhammad Shazlly Sulaiman, 34, said the incident occurred while he and his workers were tending to the inundated kitchen before the venomous reptile emerged. The trader at Jalan Balai Raya, Kampung Bukit Hijau, Jeram, said he had been worried about other venomous creatures like centipedes entering his shop, but had to take the risk and operate as usual. "I never imagined a cobra would enter due to the stagnant floodwaters since I started operating here nearly a year ago.

items.title: Police refer 32 Melaka election cases to AGC, including alleged seditious speeches
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Police have submitted 32 investigation papers related to the 16th Melaka State Election to the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) and are now awaiting further instructions. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said 42 police reports were received during the 14-day campaign period, on issues including the tearing down and burning of flags, as well as speeches by several individuals alleged to have contained seditious elements. The 16th Melaka State Election involves 28 state assembly seats.

items.title: [UNOFFICIAL] Melaka polls: PH leads in four seats
items.summary: In Ayer Keroh, PH candidate Kerk Chee Yee is leading with 1,450 votes, ahead of Perikatan Nasional's Datuk Seri Michael Gan, who has secured 420 votes. Bersama's Muhaimin Lau has received 55 votes, while Bersatu's Mohd Hamnaim has 54 votes. In Kesidang, PH's Allex Seah Shoo Chin is leading with 1225 votes, followed by PN's Albert Kok with 303 votes and Bersama's Dr Bryan Kek with 99 votes.

items.title: Myanmar airstrike on displaced persons camp kills 12
items.summary: PONNAGYUN: A Myanmar military airstrike on a camp housing people displaced by the civil war killed 12 people in the westernmost state of Rakhine, witnesses and a rescue worker said on Saturday. Chit Su Wai, a 27-year-old shopkeeper, sobbed as she described how her daughter, aunt and mother were killed on Friday evening in Byar La IDP camp in Ponnagyun township, northeast of the state capital, Sittwe. And we were lost with crying," she said.

items.title: At the Supreme Court, Trump aims to cut the power of judges again
items.summary: NEW YORK: When President Donald Trump's administration convinced the US Supreme Court last year to restrict the ability of federal judges to block his actions nationwide — a major boost to his power — the ruling left untouched a separate tool that some judges have used to stymie presidential policies. An appeal filed by Trump's Justice Department, now pending before the Supreme Court, urges the justices to curtail the longstanding ability of judges to halt the actions of federal agencies that hold immense power to carry out the Republican president's policy priorities. Siding with Trump "would give more flexibility to the executive branch", Bamzai said.

items.title: [UNOFFICIAL] BN-PN lead in 23 seats as of 7pm
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional, together with its electoral partner Perikatan Nasional, is leading in several constituencies in the Melaka election, according to unofficial results. As of 7pm, BN was leading in Kuala Linggi, Tanjung Bidara, Ayer Limau, Lendu, Durian Tunggal, Asahan, Rembia, Gadek, Sungai Udang, Klebang, Pengkalan Batu, Duyong, Telok Mas, Rim, Serkam, Merlimau and Sungai Rambai. PN, meanwhile, was leading in Paya Rumput, Ayer Keroh, Bukit Katil and Bemban.

items.title: Sarawak seeks to become technology creator in AI-driven economy
items.summary: Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said developing homegrown technological capabilities was crucial to ensuring Sarawakians did not merely benefit from digital advances but also played a leading role in shaping future industries. He said achieving this ambition required a highly skilled workforce, particularly engineers, researchers, data scientists, software developers and cybersecurity specialists who could develop and manage emerging technologies. Abang Johari said growing international investor confidence in Sarawak's economic development model reflected the state's potential to emerge as a regional hub for advanced technologies, including AI and quantum computing.

items.title: Learn from Indonesia, tighten export monitoring to stop under-invoicing, say industry players
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Stricter monitoring of commodity exports is needed to curb under-invoicing, a practice in which exporters declare lower cargo values or quantities than what they actually ship, potentially causing losses in government revenue, maritime industry players said. Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said Indonesia’s move to set up a centralised agency to monitor major commodity exports should remind Malaysia to review how effective its own export monitoring systems are. Jeyenderan said Malaysia already had various electronic systems and government agencies responsible for monitoring export declarations, permits and supporting documents.

items.title: Melaka polls: 70.59pc of ordinary voters cast their ballots
items.summary: MELAKA: A total of 70.59 per cent of ordinary voters cast their ballots in the Melaka election. The EC had set a voter turnout target of 70 per cent for the 16th Melaka election. In the 2021 state election, voter turnout stood at 65.85 per cent.

items.title: 'Tapirs also have the right to live': Dead tapir found in Ijok
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR: A tapir believed to have drowned has been found at an oil palm plantation in flood-hit Block C, Ijok. The incident was shared by Ijok state assemblyman Jefri Mejan in a Facebook post today. Jefri said a friend, identified as Andong, had sent him photographs of the animal while harvesting oil palm fruit at his plantation.

items.title: Shuhaily remains in MCBA post pending further instructions, says IGP
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain is continuing in his post pending further instructions, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said. Khalid said he had yet to receive any directive on whether Shuhaily would be returned to the police. He said Shuhaily, a police officer, was serving a two-year contract as MCBA director-general following his appointment by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

items.title: [Unofficial] Melaka polls: BN leads in four Melaka seats, PN ahead in Bukit Katil
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional (BN) is leading in four constituencies while Perikatan Nasional (PN) is ahead in Bukit Katil, said Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki based on unofficial election results. BN leads in Lendu (162 votes), Machap Jaya (57 votes), Asahan (156 votes)and Sungai Udang (6340 votes), while PN is ahead of Pakatan Harapan (PH) in Bukit Katil with 462 votes garnered. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Melaka polls: 70.23 per cent voter turnout recorded as at 5.30pm
items.summary: Based on preliminary data released by the Election Commission (EC) through its ElectionData.MY portal, state constituency N26 Serkam recorded the highest voter turnout at 79.45 per cent. State constituency N22 Bandar Hilir recorded the lowest turnout, at 57.43 per cent. Earlier, early voting recorded a high turnout of 94.96 per cent, with 9,417 of the 9,917 eligible early voters casting their ballots.

items.title: Malaysia must move beyond manufacturing and build its own brands
items.summary: Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said design was a key driver in strengthening the country's industrial capabilities. Sim said the increasingly competitive global landscape required Malaysia to move away from cost-based competition towards developing high-value products, making design an economic necessity. He said the creative economy could also generate greater added value for the country's industrial sector, particularly in the digital era.

items.title: US proposed ceding Ukrainian territory in exchange for joining Nato: Zelenskyy
items.summary: KYIV: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the United States proposed that Ukraine cede land to Russia in exchange for joining Nato, and that his government was in talks on "specific" security guarantees from the West. "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?'

items.title: No disruption to border control agency after director-general’s transfer, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: LUMUT, Nov 14 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) continues to operate as usual nationwide, unaffected by the decision to return its director-general to his parent organisation, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM). That is not how it should be,” he told reporters after officiating the Madani Kita Programme (PMK) and the 2026 handover ceremony for the People’s Volunteer Corps’ (Rela) Kampung Angkat Madani (Madani Adopted Village) and Sekolah Angkat Madani (Madani Adopted School) initiatives at Kampung Sungai Tiram here today. On October 29, the Home Ministry decided that AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain would return to duty with the PDRM.

items.title: Equal access to house arrest? That’s not Home Ministry’s call, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: LUMUT, Nov 14 — The Home Ministry acts solely as the implementing agency for the Pardons Board’s decisions on a prisoner’s sentence, including house arrest. Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry was not in a position to comment further on calls from various quarters regarding eligibility for house arrest, as pardon petitions fall outside its jurisdiction. Whether the sentence is reduced, set aside, or the person is released or placed under house arrest, our job is to implement it,” he told reporters.

items.title: (LIVE) 2026 Melaka State Election: BN-PN up in 15 seats, DAP holds strong in Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — [7.15pm] BN is ahead in 13 of the 20 seats reporting so far, PH leads in five and PN in two, and Bersama is not leading in any of them. [6.00pm] Melaka voters cast their ballots today to elect a new state legislative assembly, in a high-stakes election that serves as a critical test of Barisan Nasional's (BN) traditional fortress and the increasingly strained federal partnership between it and Pakatan Harapan (PH). PH mounted the widest campaign by fielding 24 contenders, closely followed by BN with 23 candidates.

items.title: Saifuddin: Home Ministry only implements house arrest decisions
items.summary: LUMUT: The Home Ministry is responsible for implementing decisions on house arrest but does not decide on pardon petitions or determine eligibility. "Whether a petition is submitted, discussed, considered or decided upon does not fall within the Home Ministry's area of responsibility. Also present were Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman and Rela director-general Datuk Rosli Yaakub.

items.title: Panther trapped after raiding durian orchard in Jelebu
items.summary: JELEBU: A male adult black panther weighing about 27kg was captured in Kampung Purun this morning, after a nearly three-week wait. State Perhilitan director Wan Mat Wan Harun said the department received a report on July 8 about the animal's presence at a durian orchard. He said the complainant suspected the black panther had preyed on chickens kept at the orchard.

items.title: 1,787 flood victims remain at relief centres in 3 states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,787 flood victims from 480 families are still taking shelter at 12 temporary relief centres (PPS) in three states as at 5pm today. Selangor recorded the highest number, with 1,531 victims from 410 families taking shelter at eight PPS in the Kuala Selangor district. In Perak, 220 victims from 64 families are staying at two PPS in the Hilir Perak district.

items.title: [LIVE] Melaka election results: BN-PN lead in 23 seats, PH in four
items.summary: 7.35pm - Sungai Udang - BN's Datuk Rais Yasin extends his lead with 10,843 votes. 7.29pm - Klebang - BN's Datuk Wira Lim Ban Hong is leading with 1,737 votes. 7.26pm - Serkam - BN's Datuk Azman Abdullah is leading with 3,611 votes.

items.title: Melaka turnout hits EC’s 70pc target 50 minutes before polls close
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Voter turnout for the Melaka state election reached the 70 per cent targeted by the Election Commision (EC) by 5.10pm today, ahead of polls closing at 6pm. EC real-time Voter Turnout Monitoring dashboard showed that 468,500 voters, or 70 per cent, had cast their ballots by then in the contest involving 79 candidates across 28 state seats. Serkam continued to lead with a turnout of 79.08 per cent, followed by Ayer Molek at 78.57 per cent, Tanjung Bidara at 75.94 per cent and Sungai Rambai at 75.83 per cent shortly after 5pm.

items.title: Shafie: Borneo Bloc must deliver concrete action for Sabah
items.summary: Warisan president Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal said efforts to unite the voices of Sabahans should go beyond political cooperation. He said unity must be followed by action to realise the state's rights and interests. Shafie said decades of voicing Sabah's demands would bring little change if outstanding issues continued to be delayed without resolution.

items.title: Wedding day meets polling day as Melaka newlyweds cast votes in traditional red attire
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Nov 14 — A newlywed couple made their wedding day even more memorable by taking time to cast their votes in the 16th Melaka state election today, arriving at the polling centre in their traditional red wedding attire. Yau Wei Ming, 31, and his wife Chan Jia Lin, 27, headed to Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Machap Baru here after their wedding ceremony at a temple. Yau Wei Ming, 31, and his wife Chan Jia Lin, 27, pose for a photograph after voting in the 16th Melaka state election at SJKC Machap Baru in Melaka, November 14, 2026.

items.title: Seven impact marks, metal pellets found: Police probe suspected shooting at Sarikei business premises
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 14 — Police are investigating a suspected shooting incident after a business premises’ metal shutter was found with seven impact marks along Jalan Repok, Sarikei. Sarikei District Police Chief Supt Aswandy Anis said the premises owner lodged a report at 8.30pm on November 13 after hearing seven impact sounds coming from the direction of the shop’s folding metal shutter. Aswandy said preliminary investigations found two fragments of suspected metal pellets on the walkway outside the premises.

items.title: Anwar says legacy debts like 1MDB pushed up Malaysia’s debt, cautions that corruption ruins nations
items.summary: Anwar said the government had steadily reduced its budget deficit since he became finance minister in 2022, cutting the gap between spending and revenue from about RM100 billion that year to around RM90 billion, RM80 billion and RM70 billion in the following years. “It increased because have to pay old debts — 1MDB debt, Felda debt, I have to pay RM980 million per year; Tabung Haji debt, RM10 billion have to pay,” he said. The gap between government expenditure and revenue fell from RM100.84 billion in 2022 to RM92.44 billion in 2023, RM80.9 billion in 2024 and RM76.6 billion in 2025, but is projected to rise to RM80.5 billion this year before easing to around RM79 billion next year.

items.title: Ramanan: RM1mil in aid for 1,500 flood-hit families in Sg Buloh
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH: Almost RM1 million in aid has been distributed to 1,500 families affected by floods in seven areas around Sungai Buloh under the Santuni Madani Kasih programme. He said the aid comprised household essentials, including electrical appliances worth RM625 for each affected family. "The recipients are residents of Kampung Melayu Subang, Kampung Kubu Gajah, Kampung Paya Jaras Hilir, Kampung Merbau Sempak, Kampung Sungai Pelong and Kampung Paya Jaras Tengah.

items.title: PM: Cyber, intrusion and terror threats top Malaysia’s security agenda as attacks hit thousands monthly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Malaysia is currently facing thousands of cyber attack attempts every month, thereby demanding a faster and more robust level of preparedness from security forces in confronting new-millennium defence threats. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that the country’s security landscape is no longer focused solely on conventional military threats; instead, cyber attacks, system intrusions, and terrorist cell movements have become the most critical challenges today. Therefore, we must strengthen (our defence), and last week I met with the top leadership of the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM) to discuss strengthening the cyber security unit within the Armed Forces,” he said.

items.title: Food security a national development priority - Fadillah
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said global developments had highlighted how vulnerable food supply chains can be to external disruptions, rising production costs and climate-related challenges. "We must therefore continue strengthening domestic food production while building more resilient and sustainable food systems. TAGS: food, security, Fadillah Yusof, national © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Thunderstorms, strong winds to hit seven states, KL and Putrajaya until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds across seven states, as well as the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, effective until 6pm today. In Perak, the affected areas include Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, and Manjung. A similar warning has been issued for Selangor, covering Klang, Kuala Langat, Sepang, Petaling, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, and Gombak as well as Negeri Sembilan in Port Dickson.

items.title: Police have investigated suspected AI chip transshipment since April 2025, says Saifuddin
items.summary: LUMUT: Police have been investigating allegations that Malaysia was used as a transit hub for the re-export of high-tech artificial intelligence (AI) chips since April 2025, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said. He said the investigation was conducted under the Strategic Trade Act, with the police also serving on the Strategic Trade Action Committee (STAC) under the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti). "Police opened an investigation paper as early as April 2025.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB confirms withdrawing letter to Rulers, maintains status quo of Tunku Muhriz
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 14 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has confirmed the withdrawal of the contents of a letter submitted to the Malay Rulers dated September 17 as well as the position previously taken by members of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (MMK) and effectively maintains the status quo regarding the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Also present were the Undang of Luak Rembau, Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, and the Undang of Luak Jelebu, Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi. The letter states that Ismail, together with 10 members of the State Executive Council (Exco), has unanimously decided to retract the contents of a letter dated September 17.

items.title: As smog hangs over Lahore, Pakistan's new pollution squad races to douse stubble fires
items.summary: LAHORE: As smog again settles over large parts of South Asia, Pakistani authorities are widening a crackdown on illegal stubble burning, which they say is fuelling the region's annual pollution crisis. Carrot and stick approach Silwat Saeed, chief of the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department in Pakistan's Punjab, said the government this year formed a 750-member force in 67 rapid-response units across major rice-growing districts. Farmers caught burning stubble face fines of 15,000 Pakistani rupees (US$54) per acre, said Muhammad Farooq, an assistant director of the Punjab Agriculture Department.

items.title: Slowest seat in Melaka? A look at the Bandar Hilir vote
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Bandar Hilir recorded the lowest turnout among Melaka’s 28 state constituencies, at just under 56 per cent as of 4.30pm today. The seat has 23,042 registered voters, with women making up 52 per cent of voters and men 48 per cent. Chinese voters make up about 73 per cent of the electorate, followed by Malays at 12.9 per cent, Indians at 6.4 per cent and others at 6.8 per cent.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin graces Perak-level Deepavali celebration
items.summary: IPOH: Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah and Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim attended the Perak-level Deepavali celebration at Stadium Indera Mulia. Raja Muda of Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa and Raja Di Hilir of Perak Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah also attended the event. Saarani said the Indian community's heritage in Perak was also reflected in education, culture and religion.

items.title: Melaka turnout closes in on 70pc target with over an hour of voting left
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Voter turnout in the Melaka state election reached 67.74 per cent as of 4.30pm today, approaching the Election Commission’s (EC) 70 per cent target with 90 minutes left before polling closes. Serkam continued to lead with a turnout of 77.21 per cent, followed by Ayer Molek at 76.14 per cent, Tanjung Bidara at 73.99 per cent and Sungai Rambai at 73.79 per cent. Bandar Hilir recorded the lowest turnout at 55.58 per cent, followed by Kota Laksamana at 60.20 per cent and Sungai Udang at 61.08 per cent.

items.title: Foreign minister: Malaysia urges Asean, China to redouble efforts to finalise South China Sea code
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 14 — Malaysia has urged Asean and China to show renewed political will and step up efforts to finalise the draft South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC). Asean and China are aiming to conclude negotiations on the South China Sea COC by the end of 2026. He said Asean senior officials were discussing two proposals under a mandate from Asean leaders at the 48th Asean Summit in May.

items.title: Thunderstorms and heavy rain in 7 states, KL and Putrajaya until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds across seven states, as well as the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, effective until 6pm today. In Perak, the affected areas include Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, and Manjung. A similar warning has been issued for Selangor, covering Klang, Kuala Langat, Sepang, Petaling, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, and Gombak as well as Negri Sembilan in Port Dickson.

items.title: Saifuddin: No disruption to MCBA operations amid director-general's legal case
items.summary: LUMUT: The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency continues to carry out its duties without disruption despite the legal proceedings involving its director-general, says Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said issues involving the agency's top leadership should not bring the entire organisation to a standstill or affect its responsibilities. Saifuddin said he had instructed Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman to give special attention to managing the situation, which was unprecedented.

items.title: National unity minister calls for year-round community bonding at national Deepavali celebration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Open houses, social visits and neighbourly ties should be cultivated throughout the year, rather than only during festive seasons, said National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang. He was speaking at the 2026 national-level Deepavali celebration at Little India, Brickfields here today, officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The event, organised by the Ministry of National Unity in collaboration with the Malaysian Associated Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MAICCI), was also attended by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh.

items.title: After nearly a decade, 647 Sri Pahang Flat residents closer to new homes, says Fahmi
items.summary: Lembah Pantai Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the session, held at the Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) Training Institute, marked another important step before they moved into their new homes. Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said he greatly appreciated the residents’ patience and cooperation throughout the redevelopment process. Fahmi said Residensi Maarof was scheduled to be officially opened by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in the near future.

items.title: 'I may lose my mind': Frustrated travelers stuck in US flight havoc
items.summary: I wish they had another flight, I wish I could get another flight, like, now." One airline staffer said the ground stop would last eight hours. Another said 24 hours.

items.title: Asean nations sign digital economy framework agreement to deepen economic integration
items.summary: MANILA: Asean nations on Saturday signed the landmark Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA), a pact aimed at making it easier for businesses to trade online and reach customers across the region. She said DEFA could help double the region's digital economy from an estimated US$1 trillion to US$2 trillion by 2030. The agreement, she said, provides a common framework for cross-border e-commerce, electronic payments and data flows, helping businesses reach customers across the region and giving consumers greater confidence in online transactions.

items.title: Women deserve equal chances to lead in security, defence, Anwar says, citing exam results
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said it would be unfair if women were not given equal opportunities to take on leadership roles. However, he acknowledged that women could also take on physically demanding duties. “While we give space to women, there are also duties where there are many women, in education and medical.

items.title: PM fulfils SK Polis Depot pupil’s invitation, attends school’s Anak Malaysia Carnival
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The wish of a pupil of Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Polis Depot to invite Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to attend a programme at his school came true today when the country’s top leader took time to drop by the Anak Malaysia Carnival organised by the school. Despite his hectic schedule, Anwar said he made the visit to fulfil the invitation from the pupil, identified as Muadz, while also taking the opportunity to personally inspect the school’s infrastructure and safety needs. Anwar said during his visit to the school, located within the Police Training Centre (Pulapol) in Jalan Semarak, he also took time to hear directly from the headmaster about several matters requiring attention, particularly the condition of the school’s facilities and the comfort and safety of the pupils.

items.title: Motorist slashed, kicked in Penang road rage attack; suspect jailed eight months
items.summary: Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police detected a video of the assault circulating on social media today. He said investigations found that the incident occurred about 2.07pm, involving the victim and a 30-year-old man. Rozak said the attack stemmed from the suspect's dissatisfaction with the victim's driving.

items.title: ‘We place so much hope in you’: Anwar urges NS trainees to shape Malaysia’s future
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today told National Service Training Programme 3.0 trainees that the country is placing great hope in them to secure Malaysia’s future. As he ended his hour-long speech and dialogue session with the trainees, Anwar lowered his voice to deliver his closing message. Anwar was speaking during a meet-up at the National Service Training Branch, Camp 515 here where 236 female trainees were present in-person, while another 1,663 trainees at seven other training camps joined the session online via video conference.

items.title: ‘I want to survive as a Malaysian leader’: Anwar firm in not yielding to pressure for policies based on racial dominance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has asserted that he will not bow to pressure from certain quarters seeking to alter national policies to favour racial dominance, solely for the sake of political survival. “Nowadays, wherever I go, people tell me, ‘Anwar, you must adjust the policy, it must be Malay, Malay dominance. Also present were Minister of National Unity Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang, Minister of Communications Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, and president of the Malaysian Associated Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MAICCI) Datuk Seri N. Gobalakrishnan.

items.title: At national Deepavali event, Anwar says govt committed to addressing issues affecting Indian community
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The government remains committed to addressing issues affecting the Indian community in Malaysia, particularly those related to education and welfare, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said the government acknowledged that more needed to be done to effectively address the needs of the Indian community, particularly in education. The celebration, organised by the National Unity Ministry in collaboration with the Malaysian Associated Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MAICCI), was also attended by National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Human Resource Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh.

items.title: Malaysia proposes Sustainable Haze Fund, science diplomacy for transboundary haze fight at Asean meeting, says Tok Mat
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 14 — Malaysia has called for a more proactive and coordinated Asean response to transboundary haze, advancing proposals for scientific cooperation and a Sustainable Haze Fund to strengthen the region’s preparedness. “Moving forward, Asean must pursue a more proactive and coordinated regional response, anchored in the effective implementation of the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. “Complementing these efforts, Malaysia has advanced proposals on Science Diplomacy and a Sustainable Haze Fund, to strengthen scientific cooperation, sustainable financing, and collective response to transboundary haze pollution,” he said in his intervention at the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting (AMM) here today.

items.title: Son remanded for seven days over mother’s strangling in Banting; tests positive for meth
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 14 — A man suspected of strangling his mother to death at a house in Banting, Kuala Langat, yesterday has been remanded for seven days beginning today to facilitate police investigations. Kuala Langat district police chief Supt Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi confirmed in a brief WhatsApp message that a remand order had been issued against the suspect, who is in his 20s, effective until next Friday (November 20). Mohd Akmalrizal said police were alerted to the incident at about 1pm.

items.title: SAR for final victim of Sungai Pertak water surge resumes this morning
items.summary: Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (Operations) Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the operation resumed as early as 8 am, with the deployment of the K9 Detection Dog Unit to conduct a search in Sector C. He said the operation team was also conducting surface searches in identified areas using boats. Ashrul Riezal said a total of 29 personnel from the Selangor JBPM, Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and Malaysian Civil Defence Force (APM) were involved in today’s operation. He said the search also involved six boats from the Selangor JBPM, APM and PDRM, as well as a drone.

items.title: A secret transit hub for Nvidia AI chips? Minister says Malaysian police on the case since April
items.summary: SITIAWAN, Nov 14 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) opened an investigation as early as April 2025 into US allegations that Malaysia is being used as a transit point for illicitly diverted advanced chips, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today. Saifuddin said the investigation is carried out under the Strategic Trade Act 2010. Anwar said Malaysia would cooperate with all agencies involved.

items.title: Education Ministry committed to streamlining school construction approvals, especially aided schools, says deputy minister
items.summary: Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said the ministry would help resolve issues related to documentation and administrative procedures once matters concerning sites and school enrolment needs had been settled. Also present were Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow, Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin and Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying. Citing the SJKC Heng Ee project as an example, Wong said MOE approved the school’s relocation in June 2025 after meeting representatives of its School Management Board in August 2024.

items.title: First university teaching hospital in Johor: RM900m USIM facility to be built in Sedili, says Khaled Nordin
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Nov 14 — The construction project of the Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia (USIM) Teaching Hospital (HPU), valued at RM900 million, is expected to commence next year in Sedili here in an effort to provide health services and conduct medical research focusing on rural residents. Mohamed Khaled said that currently most teaching hospitals are concentrated in the Klang Valley, including Universiti Malaya (UM), Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM), Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) and MAHSA, with research likely more focused on health issues of the urban population. He said that the construction of the USIM HPU would also make it the first university teaching hospital in Johor, thereby expanding medical research facilities to the state.

items.title: Atmaca: Additional cost for LCS involves integration and launcher system, refund from Norway to pay for missiles, says minister
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Nov 14 — The additional costs arising from the use of the Turkish-made Atmaca missile for the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) littoral combat ships (LCS) pertain to integration work and the launcher system, said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. “I had already ordered the Atmaca missiles for LMS. “The costs involve integration and the launcher system (additional costs).

items.title: Khaled Nordin: Malaysia to receive all 18 FA-50M fighter jets by March 2028 to replace RMAF’s ageing Hawk fleet
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Nov 14 — Malaysia is expected to receive all 18 FA-50M light combat aircraft from South Korea by March 2028 to strengthen the country’s air defence capabilities. The remaining 12 aircraft are expected to be delivered by March 2028, completing the procurement. Malaysia signed a contract with Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI) in 2023 to procure 18 FA-50M aircraft for nearly RM4 billion under the 12th Malaysia Plan.
